raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 45 years, and at 63, I know every inch of my 7 mu. It's just my wife and me at home now—our child works off-farm at a factory in town, so the two of us manage everything. Cotton has been our crop for as long as I can remember. The soil here is decent, and I've got my well for irrigation when the rains don't cooperate, which they often don't on the North China Plain.

This year, I'm putting all 7 mu into cotton again. Some folks talk about rotating, but with only 7 mu and cotton prices stable enough, I stick with what I know best. I'll buy hybrid seeds from the county supply shop—the new varieties give better boll weight and hold up better against disease. I stopped saving my own seeds years ago; the hybrids are worth every yuan.

For fertilizer, I'll apply about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium. After decades of cotton, I know this soil doesn't need more than that—too much nitrogen and the plants grow too tall, drop their bolls, and attract more pests. I'll split the nitrogen, putting half down at planting and the rest at flowering time.

Water will make or break the crop. I plan to irrigate four times from my well: once right after planting to get good emergence, again at flowering when the plants are thirsty, a third time at peak boll-setting, and a fourth in August if the summer turns dry. My well has never let me down, and I don't intend to let the crop suffer.

Pests are a constant battle here—bollworm, aphids, red spider mite. I'll spray five times this season, starting early and staying ahead of them. I don't like the cost of the chemicals, but losing half the crop to worms is worse.

For tillage, I'll do rotary tillage in spring to break up the soil and prepare a good seedbed. No-tillage doesn't work for cotton around here; the ground gets too hard and the roots can't dig deep.

If the weather cooperates and I stay on top of the watering and spraying, I expect to harvest around 320 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year was a bit dry, but I still pulled nearly 300 kg per mu. With careful management and the hybrid variety, 320 kg is a fair target.
